title: The Snowflake Hypothesis: Training and Powering GNN with One Node One Receptive Field

problem.claim: Deep GNNs face significant overfitting and over-smoothing issues.

gap.claim: Existing approaches often lack intrinsic interpretability and treat all nodes within a layer similarly, failing to capture differences among nodes.

contributions.claim: Introduces the Snowflake Hypothesis, a paradigm based on assigning one receptive field to each node.

stated_novelty.claim: The Snowflake Hypothesis is presented as a novel paradigm.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that deep GNN success primarily derives from CNN-inspired innovations such as residual or skip connections and tailor-made aggregation algorithms such as DropEdge.

narrative_sequence.summary: Deep GNNs encounter overfitting and over-smoothing as they become deeper.
The authors conduct a systematic study of deep GNN models and attribute their current success mainly to CNN-derived innovations or specialized aggregation algorithms.
These approaches are described as lacking intrinsic interpretability and treating nodes uniformly within layers.
The paper introduces the Snowflake Hypothesis based on one node having one receptive field.

source_observation.claim: Uniform treatment of nodes within a layer may fail to capture node-level differences.

interpretation.claim: Node-specific receptive fields may be a useful design direction for addressing limitations of deep GNNs.

application.claim: When designing deep graph models, consider mechanisms that adapt receptive fields to individual nodes.

exception.claim: The supplied abstract does not establish whether node-specific receptive fields improve performance or interpretability.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the proposed method or implementation details.
The abstract does not report experiments, datasets, quantitative results, or comparisons.
